chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"Saturday is for Banī Hāshim, and Sunday is for Banī Umayyah, so beware of taking Sunday."

key_terms.السَّبْتُ: Saturday, mentioned here as specially associated with Banī Hāshim
key_terms.الْأَحَدُ: Sunday, mentioned here as associated with Banī Umayyah
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: the clan of Hāshim, the family line of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.فَاتَّقُوا: so beware; exercise caution and God-conscious restraint

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by saying Saturday is for Banī Hāshim and Sunday is for Banī Umayyah?
ai.summary: Imam عليه السلام assigns symbolic distinction to Saturday and Sunday, associating Saturday with Banī Hāshim and Sunday with Banī Umayyah. The statement functions as a caution against adopting or preferring what is linked to Banī Umayyah in this context, within the discussion of Jumu'ah and related devotional practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Saturday is for the Banu Hashim, and Sunday is for the Banu Umayyah, so beware of taking Sunday”.
